James  Pillsbury  Lane,  of  Massachusetts,  studied  for  a   "■   V'   period  of  twenty  years  the  general  history  of  the   Lane  families  of  y    New  England.     He  published   "Ancestry  of  Dea.  Joshua  Lane  of   ^   ...     Hampton,  N.  H."  in  1SS5  ;   "Lane   Families  of  the  Massachusetts   ^""n^  Bay  Colony"  in  1SS6;  "James  Lane  of  North  Yarmouth,  Me.,  and  His  Descendants "  in  18SS.  It  was  Mr.  Lane's  ambition  to  publish  a  complete  genealogy  of  the  several  New  England  families.  His  work,  incomplete  at  his  death  in  1SS9,  was  too  valuable  to  be  lost.  His  manuscripts  have  been  carefully  verified  in  nearly  all  particulars.   The  Hon.  Ebenezer  Lane  of  Ohio  spent  much  time  in  looking  up  the  family  of  William  Lane  of  Dorchester,  Mass.  He  visited  England  in  1S59  and  i860,  where  he  discovered  an  old  home  of  the  Lane  family  in  the  central  part  of  Norfolkshire.  There  he  saw  monuments  in  the  church  and  tombstones  in  the  churchyard  with  the  name  Lane  upon  them.  He  went  into  Lane  Hall  where  the  family  resided.  It  was  then  owned  by  Mr.  Lewis,  who  had  married  the  Lane  heiress  and  was  hving  in  Rome  to  educate  their  children.  Mr.  Lane's  "  Imperfect  List  of  Descendants,  etc.,"  was  an  early  attempt  to  publish  a  family  history.    \^    iv  rKF.FACE.   Charles  Benjamin  West  Lane,  Esq.,  deposited  a  manuscript  sketch  of  the  Lane  family  of  Hingham,  Mass.,  with  the  New  Eng-  land Historic  Genealogical  Society,  Boston.  His  son,  Mr.  Charles  Andrew  Lane,  visited  Hingham,  England,  in  the  summer  of  1891,  and  saw  Lane  monuments  in  the  churchyard  there.   Mrs.  i\Lary  Avis  (Hodges)  Lane,  secretary  of  the  annual  Lane  Gathering  at  Norton,  Mass.,  has  been  untiring  in  collecting  mate-  rials relating  to  the  families  in  that  vicinity. history.  Elisha  Frederick  Lane,  Esq.,  of  New  Hampshire  has  contributed  gleanings  for  the  families  in  the  vicinity  of  Svvanzey,  N.  H.   The  history  of  Robert  Lane  of  Stratford,  Conn.,  and  his  de-  scendants has  been  enthusiastically  pursued  by  Theodore  Freling-  huysen  Lane  and  John  Nelson  Lane,  Esqs.,  of  Connecticut.  Mr.  Abner  Lane  of  Connecticut  secured  a  careful  list  of  the  Killing-  worth  Lanes  from  the  town  records  about  i860.  Dea.  Charles  Lane  of  Ohio  has  furnished  accurate  lists  of  a  score  of  Ohio  fam-  ilies connected  with  the  branch.  Bela  Chapin,  A.  i\L,  of  New  Hampshire  has  added  to  other  literary  work  this  labor  of  love,  to  look  up  his  Lane  ancestry  and  print  appreciative  sketches  of  the  families  in  Newport,  N.  H.  The  late  David  Williams  Patterson,  Esq.,  of  New  York,  left  'a  manuscript  history  of  Robert  Lane  and  his  descendants,  1665-1862,  too  valuable  to  be  lost.   Grenville  Howland  Norcross,  Esq.,  of  Massachusetts,  furnished  almost  entirely  the  sketch  of  his  ancestor,  John  Merrifield  Lane  of  Boston,  Mass.   Rev.  John  William  Lane  has  extended  his  helpful  interest  be-  yond his  particular  clan.   Many  other  persons  have  given  accounts  of  their  several  fami-  lies. This  volume  could  not  have  been  prepared  without  such  cordial  assistance.  It  has  been  a  labor  of  love  for  the  living,  of  reverence  for  the  departed,  of  help  and  of  hope  for  the  coming  generations.   Newfif.lds,  N.  H.,  February,  1897. William  Lane  of  Dorchester,  Mass.,  1635,   AND    DESCENDANTS.    The  settlement  at  Mattapan,  on  Massachusetts  Bay,  was  incorpor-  ated by  the  name  of  Dorchester,  Sept.  7,  1630.  The  first  inhabi-  tants were  chiefly  from  the  counties  of  Devon,  Dorset,  and  Somer-  set, England.  "They  came  to  .America  for  the  purpose  of  enjoying  those  religious  privileges  which  the  measures  of  Archbishop  Laud  denied  them  at  home." — Dorc'tu-sUr   Church  Records. M.  Harris. March  18,  he  had  two  additional  grants  of  between  si.x  and  seven  acres.
